description: Use when a report or dashboard is slow, timing out, hitting row limits, or consuming excessive system resources on large-volume objects — covers selective filter strategy, custom report type optimization, async report execution via Analytics API, dashboard refresh scheduling, and grouping/aggregation tuning. Triggers: 'report times out', 'report is slow', 'dashboard not refreshing', 'report row limit hit', 'too many report results'. NOT for CRM Analytics / Tableau CRM performance (separate skill). NOT for sharing-model or visibility issues causing missing rows (use admin/sharing-and-visibility). NOT for building or designing reports from scratch (use admin/reports-and-dashboards-fundamentals).
inputs: The report or dashboard name and the primary object it is built on
Approximate record volume on the primary object (orders of magnitude sufficient)
Current filters applied — or confirmation that no filters exist
Report type: standard or custom, and how many objects are spanned
Whether the report is run interactively, on subscription, via dashboard, or via API
name: report-performance-tuning
official_sources: Large Data Volumes Best Practices — selectivity and indexes for reports (ldv 264 L225-226), index thresholds (L463, L468), fields indexed by default (L308-309), full scan without an index (L305-307), Reporting best practices (L787-811), multi-join report case (L1240-1260).

Reports and Dashboards REST API Developer Guide 262 — Requirements and Limitations ("The API returns up to the first 2,000 report rows", 1,200 async and 500 sync runs per hour, 100 columns, 200 dashboard refreshes per hour, 5 report subscriptions per user); Run Reports Synchronously or Asynchronously (2-minute timeout does not apply to async, 24-hour results); Report Error Codes (100-column message); Instances List (`New`/`Running`/`Success`/`Error`) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_analytics.meta/api_analytics/sforce_analytics_rest_api_limits_limitations.htm

Metadata API Developer Guide — Report fields `crossFilters`, `description`, `scope`, `timeFrameFilter` and `ReportFilter.booleanFilter` (api_meta 264 L106680, L106706, L106812-106829, L107292-107296, L107791-107801); Dashboard `dashboardType` (L50170-50190); ReportType `ObjectRelationship` join limits and `outerJoin` (L108487-108495) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_report.htm

Apex Developer Guide — Reports and Dashboards API via Apex, Requirements and Limitations: 100 columns, 500 sync / 1,200 async runs per hour, 24-hour async results, "The API returns up to the first 2,000 report rows", 20 custom field filters, 200 dashboard refreshes per hour (apexdev 264 L33669-33694); sync rows count toward the 50,000 SOQL rows limit (L33700-33702); same record count as the UI (L33714-33715).
Object Reference — `CronJobDetail.JobType` `3` = Dashboard Refresh (obj 264 L86824, L86850); `CronTrigger.CronJobDetailId` (L86903).
Bulk API 2.0 Developer Guide — bulk queries (api_asynch 264 L136-137), query job resources (L1055-1126).

Salesforce Help (not corpus) — Improve Report Performance; Reports and Dashboards Limits and Allocations; Cross Filter Considerations; Dynamic Dashboards — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_improve_performance.htm
outputs: Filter strategy recommendation with specific fields to use (date range, owner, record type)
Report type simplification recommendation if applicable
Extraction path for result sets over 2,000 rows: filter-chunked report runs (the Reports and Dashboards REST API returns only the first 2,000 rows, sync or async) or a Bulk API 2.0 query
Dashboard refresh schedule and component count guidance (UNVERIFIED Help-only caps flagged)
Grouping and aggregation design to reduce processing overhead
